$comment: Every src/app/api/**/route.ts and src/app/(app)/**/page.tsx, classified for the Swift apps. `npm run native:parity:check` fails on a route or page missing here, on an entry whose file is gone, and on a route status the Swift contradicts (native routes must be named by a Swift string literal or carry `swift`; a route the Swift calls must be native or carry `ignoreSwift`). Route statuses: native, planned, web-only, internal. Page statuses per app (mac, ios): native, partial, planned, web-only. planned, web-only and partial need a note. `npm run native:parity` writes docs/native/PARITY_MATRIX.md from this file.

features.title: Sign-in and account security
features.note: Browser sign-in hands the apps a PKCE code; everything after that is `/api/v1/auth/*` and the account routes Settings › Account calls.

/api/account.note: Legacy: no client calls it; the web and the apps delete an account with POST /api/account/delete.

/api/account/username.note: Settings › Account › Username on both apps (DesktopUsernameRow on the Mac, JunoMobileUsernameView on the iPhone), with the web's debounced ?check= and its words; NativeUsernameClient/NativeUsernameModel in JunoChatKit/NativeUsername.swift.

/api/account/verification.note: The web's check-your-inbox banner for an unverified email; the apps do not show it yet.

/api/auth/[...nextauth].note: The web's session (Auth.js). The apps sign in through the browser and hold /api/v1/auth tokens.

/api/auth/mfa/challenge.note: The web sign-in's second factor, which the apps' browser sign-in passes through.

/api/auth/register.note: Accounts are created on the web; the apps sign in through the browser.

/api/auth/reset-password.note: The emailed reset link opens on the web; the apps ask for the email with /api/auth/forgot-password.

/api/auth/verify-email.note: The emailed verification link opens on the web.

/api/v1/auth/devices.note: Signed-in devices and their revocation. Settings › Devices lists Macs for Work, not signed-in devices.

features.title: Sync and bootstrap
features.note: The apps render from their local store and reconcile through the `/api/v1` sync contract (`contracts/openapi/juno-native-v1.yaml`).

/api/sync/changes.note: The web's own change feed; the apps sync through /api/v1/changes.

/api/sync/stream.note: The web's own wake-up stream; the apps listen on /api/v1/changes/stream.

features.title: Chat and streaming
features.note: POST /api/chat's body and frames are classified field by field in the chat wire contract (`npm run native:wire:check`).

/api/approvals/grants.note: The standing "always allow" grants listed under Customize › Apps on the web, so a person can see what Juno may do without asking. The apps answer approvals but do not list standing grants yet.

/api/approvals/grants/[id].note: Revoking one standing grant from that list (DELETE). As /api/approvals/grants.

/api/chat/clarify.note: Whether to ask a clarifying question before a turn runs; the Mac's composer has no pre-flight questions yet (request.preflightClarification in the chat wire).

/api/mentions.note: The composer's @ lookup for typed context tokens (agents, files, projects, apps with their connection and approval state, skills, chats, artifacts). Both apps' composers call it and send the chosen tokens as request.context.

/api/chat/receipt.note: Receipt refresh for a durable first submission, built for native recovery; the Swift apps append the turn first and have not adopted the durable pair (request.clientRequestId in the chat wire).

/api/models.note: The web's model list. The apps read /api/v1/models; the Electron client (native/desktop-electron) still reads this one.

/api/conversations/[id]/tasks.note: Every task a conversation draws (all live ones plus the newest finished one), for several tasks per conversation. The apps still follow the newest task through /api/work/sessions?conversationId=, which is unchanged.

/api/folders.note: The apps create and rename folders through sync (/api/v1/mutations).

/api/messages/[id].note: Edit-and-resend of a sent question, keeping the old text as a version; the Mac's question editor does not call it.

/api/share/report.note: Reporting a shared link happens on the shared page, which only the web draws.

features.title: Search and recents
features.note: The Mac's ⌘K panel searches chats, messages, projects, files and artifacts on this Mac and asks the server for memory, knowledge and tasks (register #131).

/projects.note: Folders (Project.parentId) are planned: the apps list every project flat and do not yet nest folders under their project, move one with Move to… or drag and drop, or ask whether a deleted folder's subfolders go up a level or go with it.

/projects/[id].note: Folders are planned: no breadcrumbs, Folders section or New folder yet, and the app does not show the instructions and files a folder inherits from the projects above it (the server already prepends them to its chats).

/api/projects/[id].note: The apps change projects through sync (/api/v1/mutations); only a blank-name create goes to POST /api/projects (register #89). Moving a project into a folder (PATCH parentId), the folder fields on GET (breadcrumbs, children, inherited) and DELETE ?children=lift|cascade are web-only until native folders land; a sync project.delete lifts a folder's subfolders up a level, as the web does by default.

/api/projects/[id]/members.note: Project members (sharing a project); not in the apps yet.

/knowledge/documents/[id].note: The document inspector, as a Library detail (fact-check errata, Web).

/api/attachments/[id]/document.note: The web's document viewer beside the chat; the Mac opens files in Quick Look (register #19).

/api/files/sandbox/[...key].note: Files the web's in-browser Python sandbox writes.

/api/knowledge/documents.note: Which documents became citable, and the document inspector; a Library detail on the Mac (fact-check errata, Web).

/api/library/made.note: Everything Juno made in one paged list: chat artifacts and task deliverables (docx, xlsx, pptx…), each with a kind and a type. The apps list artifacts from sync and deliverables from /api/work/artifacts.

/api/prompts.note: The saved-prompt library (insert, use counts); the apps read saved prompts through sync but have no library dialog.

features.title: Artifacts and Design
features.note: Design is a type of artifact (register #73).

/a/[id].note: The phone opens an artifact inline or in the design editor; it has no artifact page of its own.

/design.note: A redirect to Artifacts filtered to designs (register #73).

/design/[artifactId].note: A redirect to /a/{id}, the design editor.

/api/artifacts.note: The apps list artifacts from sync; the web's grid asks for previews here.

/api/artifacts/[id]/download.note: Download one version as a file, or a design (or any artifact, format=zip) as a ZIP bundle with a README and optional history. The apps still share a design's source through the system share sheet.

/api/artifacts/[id]/draft.note: Seals or discards the web design editor's working copy (ArtifactDraft). The Mac and iPhone hosted editors keep their own draft and save a whole document through /api/artifacts/[id] with a base version.

/api/artifacts/[id]/duplicate.note: Duplicate an artifact into a new one in the same project, with derivedFrom provenance. No Duplicate command in the apps yet.

/api/artifacts/[id]/proposals/[proposalI.note: Compare a held re-emit (the re-emit guard's suggestion) with the current version. The apps show neither the suggestion bar nor Compare yet; a held tag draws no card there.
Apply a held re-emit as the next version, against the version the person compared.
The picture of a suggested design, for Compare.

/api/artifacts/[id]/publication.note: The apps read an existing publication (GET) to share its live link; opening an artifact never publishes it. Publish, Update, Roll back and Unpublish stay on the web until the native lane adds the panel.

/api/artifacts/[id]/publication/reset.note: Reset a published link: the old token answers link gone, a new token serves.

/api/artifacts/[id]/restore.note: Restore from Recently deleted. A delete from the apps now moves the artifact to Recently deleted (the sync feed tombstones it); the apps have no Recently deleted view yet.

/api/artifacts/[id]/versions.note: Paginated version history (newest first, bodies on request). The apps read versions from sync and the windowed /api/artifacts/[id].

/api/artifacts/[id]/versions/[version].note: One version's body, for paged history.

/api/design/[artifactId].note: The Mac reads a design's document from its artifact and hands it to the hosted editor.

/api/design/[artifactId]/edit.note: Ask Juno to change the selected layers of a design; the Mac's hosted editor has no Ask Juno yet.

/api/design/[artifactId]/transactions.note: The web's editor commits each edit here as it goes; the Mac's host saves edits its own way and does not call it.

/api/artifacts/[id]/ops.note: Targeted edits to a semantic spreadsheet, document or deck. Native clients are given the Markdown artifact contract instead, so no semantic artifact reaches them to edit.

/api/memory/skill-candidates.note: Methods Alevr noticed the person repeat, offered as draft skills on the web's Memory page. The apps do not list them yet.

/api/memory/skill-candidates/[id].note: Accepting or dismissing a proposed skill; web first, like the list.

/customize.note: The web's Customize hub opens on its Apps tab, which renders /connections; the apps reach the same screen as Connections.

/api/connectors/usage.note: When each app was last used (tool, chat), for the app's details under Customize › Apps on the web. The apps do not show a last-used line yet.

/api/connectors/[id]/callback.note: The provider redirects the browser here; the apps start the flow at /api/connectors/{id}/connect in the browser.

/api/connectors/[id]/credentials.note: Key and token connectors (Apple Music and others) are connected on the web; the apps have no credential form yet.

/api/connectors/apple-music/dev-token.note: MusicKit JS in the browser needs it; there is no MusicKit JS in the apps.

/api/connectors/custom.note: Mac only: lists and adds an OAuth-protected MCP server by URL (DesktopCustomConnectorSheets). The iPhone shows saved ones through /api/connectors but has no add form yet.

/api/connectors/custom/probe.note: Mac only: checks a pasted URL before it is added. As /api/connectors/custom.

/api/connectors/custom/[id].note: Mac only: reads, renames, switches tools off and removes a custom server.

/api/connectors/custom/[id]/tools.note: Mac only: refreshes the server's tool list.

/api/connectors/custom/[id]/connect.swift: NativeCustomConnectorPath.connectURL(backend:id:) in JunoChatKit/NativeCustomConnectors.swift, opened in the browser
/api/connectors/custom/[id]/connect.note: Mac only: sign-in to the server starts here in the person's browser.

/api/connectors/custom/callback.note: The server's authorization page redirects the browser here; the Mac starts the flow at /api/connectors/custom/{id}/connect in the browser.

/api/mcp/[connector].note: MCP servers Juno hosts for its own model runs.

/api/mcp/servers.note: The Mac adds a custom MCP server (POST). Saved servers reach both apps as `user_mcp:` rows in /api/connectors; the iPhone has no add form yet.

/api/mcp/servers/[id].note: The Mac edits, enables and disables a custom server (PATCH); Disconnect on either app deletes one (DELETE).

/api/mcp/servers/[id]/test.note: Mac only: Test in the edit sheet for a saved server.

/api/mcp/servers/test.note: Mac only: Test in the add sheet before saving.

/skills.note: No Skills pages on the phone yet.

/skills/import.note: A sheet on the Mac; no Skills pages on the phone yet.

/api/skills/import/file.note: Mac only: previews an uploaded SKILL.md (the web parses it in the browser); no Skills pages on the phone yet.

/api/skills/import/package.note: Importing an uploaded SKILL.md or .zip/.skill package, pasted text or a public link, through the SSRF-safe fetcher. The Mac previews a SKILL.md through /api/skills/import/file; packages and links are web-only until the native lane adds them.

/api/work/skills/[id]/versions/[version].note: Reading a skill version's bundled files (skills as executable workflows, 2026-10-02); the Mac skill detail does not list them yet.

/api/work/skills/[id]/export.note: Download a skill as its SKILL.md or a zip other hosts install from. The apps have no export action yet.

/assistants.note: No Assistants page on the phone yet (a project's assistant is edited in the project).

/api/assistants/[id]/move-to-crew.note: Move to crew (D-007): the assistant becomes a crew member and leaves the list. The apps still read and open assistants; they have no Move action yet.

features.title: Tasks in chat
features.note: The web retired its task pages: a task lives in its chat (Phase 5). `/api/tasks` is the older scheduled-task store the apps still read.

/work/[[...segments]].note: Redirects into the task's chat. The phone keeps its older Work tab.

/tasks.note: A redirect to Automations. The phone keeps its scheduled Tasks list.

/api/work/artifacts/[id]/preview.note: A spreadsheet deliverable as a grid for the browser; the Mac opens deliverables in Quick Look (register #58).

/api/work/sessions/[id]/transfer.note: Hands a task to another crew member or back to the person, with a reason, at a safe point; recorded as an owner_transferred event. Web-first (crew foundations); no app screen yet.

/api/work/sessions/counts.note: The web's sidebar counts; the Mac counts the chats its column can show (register #69).

/automations.note: No Automations on the phone yet.

features.title: Permissions and this Mac as a host

/permissions.note: No Permissions page on the phone yet.

/crew.note: A user-facing alias of /agents that renders the same agents home; the apps' Agents destination is the same place.

/api/agents/[id]/computer/files.note: Agent computer file listing and download; web panel disclosure.

/api/computer-view/session.note: Called by the /computer-view page the apps open in a web view: it trades the page's one-time ticket for the viewer's credentials. The apps never call it themselves.

/api/agents/[id]/setup-changes/[changeId.note: A setup change asked for in a crew member's thread: read its live status, Apply (digest-bound) or Undo. The apps show the thread's text but not the card yet.

/api/agents/[id]/starter.note: The Mac sends a new agent's first message when its thread opens (the web reads it server-side in /chat/{id}); the iPhone does not fetch it yet.

/api/agents/[id]/undo.note: Agent event undo; wired into AgentClient.swift in Phase 7.

/api/agents/[id]/board.note: An Orbit member's work board (goals, dependencies, retries). Web first; the apps show the member's tasks without the board yet.

/api/agents/[id]/goals/[goalId]/advance.note: Advancing a durable goal by one step from the board. The apps have no board to press it from yet.

/api/agents/[id]/memory-access.note: What an Orbit member may read of the account's memory, set from its page on the web. The apps keep the default grant until they show the setting.

/api/agents/rooms.note: Orbit rooms: two to six members answering in one conversation. Web first; the apps open a room's conversation as an ordinary chat.

/api/agents/rooms/[conversationId].note: A room's members, turn plan and handoffs. The apps draw the replies without the room's bylines yet.

/research.note: A redirect to a new chat with Research armed.

/research/[id].note: A redirect to the run's chat.

features.title: Voice
features.note: Relay wire (not a route): the apps send each dial provider's thinking rung (`effort`) on session.start/switch — OpenAI low/medium/high/xhigh (GPT-6.1 Sol's effort, default high), Gemini low/medium/high (3.8 Live + Flash low, or 3.8 Live Thinking + Flash high; default low) — set on the Mac with the shared JunoThinkingPanel and in iOS Settings with JunoThinkingTrack (the iOS call menu uses a picker). Planned: reading `session.ready.effort`/`delegate`/`model`; the apps show the rung's expected model names rather than the relay's report.

/api/voice/memory.note: The web's voice call reads memory here; the apps' calls get their context from /api/voice/context.

/api/voice/stt.note: The web's dictation; the apps dictate on the device.

features.title: Juno Code
features.note: Owned by the Code rework (`docs/native/code-rework/`), which audits Code's parity; the statuses here are the Swift's calls as found, with the web-only verbs named.

/code.note: The phone supervises remote and cloud runs.

/code/pulls.note: Pull requests are listed through /api/code/github/pulls; the page itself is Code's.

/code/customize.note: Code's settings cover permissions, model, MCP, hooks, skills and agents; cloud environments are missing.

/api/agent/usage.note: Usage accounting for Juno Code's engine against the plan; the Swift engine does not report its turns here yet.

/api/code/cloud-runner.note: Whether a cloud run could start, asked when the Cloud target is chosen.

/api/code/devices/[deviceId]/sessions/[s.note: The host's detail snapshot of one session; native Code uploads the session list only.
The web's per-verb form; native Code sends the same verbs as commands (POST /api/code/devices/{deviceId}/commands).

/api/code/github/branches.note: The base-branch list for a cloud run.

/api/code/tasks/[id]/checks.note: CI checks on the pushed branch.

/api/code/tasks/[id]/pull-request.note: Open a pull request for a cloud run.

/api/code/workspaces.note: The app is meant to mirror its Code workspaces here so the web's Code tab lists them; native Code does not yet.

/customize/instructions.note: The web's Customize › Instructions tab renders the same personalization section as Settings.

/profile.screen: NativeProfileView (DesktopProfileScreen from the account menu's Profile row; JunoMobileProfileView under Settings › Account)

/api/i18n/translations.note: The web's automatic interface translation; the Mac has no interface language yet (register #124).

/api/profile/stats.note: The activity heatmap and lifetime totals in Settings › Account; the Mac shows usage from /api/profile/usage (owner question: the Mac-only usage cards).

/api/push/subscriptions.note: Browser push; the apps register through /api/v1/devices/apns.

/api/profile/activity.note: The profile page's activity read, with the reader's zone as ?tz=; NativeProfileClient in JunoChatKit/NativeProfileActivity.swift, drawn by NativeProfileView on both apps.

/api/secrets.note: The credential vault the agent computer fills sign-ins from, managed in the web's Settings. The apps do not manage it yet.

/api/secrets/[id].note: Editing or deleting one stored credential; web first, like the list.

/api/secrets/grants.note: Which sites and tasks may use a stored credential; web first.

/api/secrets/grants/[id].note: Revoking one credential grant; web first.

/upgrade.note: A sheet on the Mac, monthly only (register #127). The phone has no plan purchase yet (JunoStoreKit is in the shared package).

/upgrade/welcome.note: Where the web's in-app Stripe checkout returns after paying; the apps buy through the App Store.

/api/billing/app-store.note: The unversioned alias of /api/v1/billing/app-store; the apps call the v1 path.

/api/billing/credits.note: Mac only: the Top-ups block of Settings › Plan & usage (DesktopBillingExtras). The iPhone buys through the App Store and does not show top-ups.

/api/stripe/topup.note: Mac only: Add opens the Stripe Checkout page in the browser, like the Mac's plan checkout. App Store rules keep this purchase off the iPhone.

/api/stripe/cancel.note: Mac only: Cancel subscription with the recap and the web's consent text (DesktopCancelSubscriptionSheet), and Keep my subscription. An App Store subscription is cancelled in the App Store; the iPhone does not show it.

/api/referrals.note: Mac only: Invite a friend in Settings › Plan & usage (link, Copy, rewards). The iPhone does not show it yet.

/compare.note: Deferred (fact-check errata, Web); ⌘K leaves it out (register #132).

/roadmap.note: Roadmap & feature requests opens on the web (register #132).

/api/roadmap.note: Roadmap & feature requests opens on the web (register #132).

/api/roadmap/[id].note: Roadmap & feature requests opens on the web (register #132).

/api/roadmap/[id]/comments.note: Roadmap & feature requests opens on the web (register #132).

/api/roadmap/[id]/vote.note: Roadmap & feature requests opens on the web (register #132).

features.title: Owner tools
features.note: The owner's moderation and account tools stay on the web.

/admin/turns.note: The owner's turn trace viewer (route timing, routing receipts); an operator tool.

features.title: Platform endpoints
features.note: Health, reports, webhooks and runner endpoints no client screen calls, and the download feed the Mac's updater reads.

/api/code/tasks/[id]/controls.note: Control events for the host or cloud runner, not a client screen.

/api/code/tasks/[id]/runner-context.note: Served once to the GitHub Actions runner (OIDC only).

/api/csp-report.note: Where the browser's CSP sends violation reports.

/api/v1/billing/app-store/webhook.note: App Store Server Notifications (the v1 alias).

/api/voice/spend.note: The voice relay reports what a live call has cost.

/api/work/schedules/[id]/fire.note: Fired from outside Juno with the automation's own token.
